system_description.narrative_title: Trump–Xi summit as fulcrum for US–China AI, trade and supply‑chain diplomacy
system_description.narrative_summary: A high‑stakes state visit by China's Xi to meet President Trump is the focal event driving intense preparatory diplomacy and industry lobbying across AI governance, tariffs, rare earths/critical minerals and auto market access. Delegations and envoys (notably Scott Bessent and China's He Lifeng), corporate actors (bank, auto, tech CEOs) and markets are interacting in an open system of negotiations where policy levers, export controls and cooperative safety frameworks are being tested and sequenced in real time. Outcomes will ripple into global finance, supply chains and regional security arrangements and generate follow‑up dialogues (e.g., planned AI safety talks in Shenzhen).
system_description.scope: Bilateral US–China summit process and its immediate network: preparatory government talks (Treasury, trade, vice premiers), AI safety dialogue and norm‑setting, trade/tariff/market‑access negotiations (autos, LNG), critical minerals/rare‑earths supply and export controls, corporate lobbying and diplomatic choreography (state dinner, CEOs attending), and short‑term market and currency responses.
system_description.super_system: Global geopolitical‑economic order (US‑China strategic rivalry embedded in multilateral governance, global markets and supply chains).
adjacent_subsystems: Global tech governance and AI safety regimes
Global trade and industrial supply chains (autos, rare earths, LNG)
Global financial markets and monetary policy
Asia‑Pacific regional security and diplomacy (Taiwan, Hong Kong, APEC)

variables.name: Bilateral tariff level
variables.description: Average applied tariff rate on traded goods and services between the two negotiating economies.

variables.name: Export control stringency
variables.description: Degree of legal and administrative restrictiveness applied to cross-border transfers of sensitive technologies and inputs.

variables.name: Minerals import dependency
variables.description: Share of critical-mineral and rare-earth requirements met through external suppliers in the bilateral supply relationship.

variables.name: Rare-earth flow rate
variables.description: Volume rate of rare-earth and other critical-mineral shipments traversing the bilateral supply corridor per unit time.

variables.name: AI governance alignment
variables.description: Degree of policy and regulatory convergence on AI safety norms, standards and cooperative mechanisms between parties.

variables.name: Diplomatic negotiation intensity
variables.description: Frequency and density of preparatory talks, envoy exchanges and formal meetings in the summit and follow-up process.

variables.name: Corporate lobbying pressure
variables.description: Aggregate intensity of private-sector advocacy directed at shaping policy positions and market-access outcomes in negotiations.

variables.name: Financial market volatility
variables.description: Degree of short-term price variability and risk premia in financial markets driven by bilateral policy uncertainty.

variables.name: Currency pressure
variables.description: Directional stress on exchange-rate valuations linked to capital flows and policy signals emanating from the bilateral relationship.

variables.name: Supply-chain resilience
variables.description: Robustness of industrial supply chains to disruption, including substitution capacity and time-to-recovery for key components.

variables.name: Technology decoupling degree
variables.description: Extent of fragmentation between competing technological ecosystems, standards and interoperable infrastructures.

variables.name: Regulatory enforcement capacity
variables.description: Administrative and operational capacity to implement and enforce trade measures, export controls and safety regulations.

variables.name: Domestic political pressure
variables.description: Intensity of domestic political constraints, lobbying and public mobilization pushing negotiators toward protectionist or accommodative stances.

variables.name: Investor confidence
variables.description: Level of market participants' confidence regarding future returns and policy stability tied to the bilateral interaction.

variables.name: Negotiation concession flow
variables.description: Rate at which policy concessions, tariff adjustments or market-access commitments are offered, modified or accepted during talks.

variables.name: Strategic trust level
variables.description: Mutual strategic trust and perceived reliability between negotiating leaderships in managing shared risks and commitments.

catalysts.title: Trump–Xi summit (Xi US visit Sept 23–25)
catalysts.description: Presidential meetings and state events during Xi's US visit (Sept 23–25) that will concentrate bargaining, announcements and signaling.
catalysts.rationale: Xi visiting US Sept 23–25 concentrates talks, state dinner and high-level meetings ("China's Xi to visit the US from September 23-25", "What to expect from upcoming summit").

catalysts.title: AI safety follow-up talks in Shenzhen
catalysts.description: Planned follow-up AI safety meetings in Shenzhen roughly two months after the summit, continuing regulatory dialogue and technical coordination.
catalysts.rationale: Officials announced another AI safety meeting in about two months in Shenzhen ("US, China to meet again on AI safety in two months in Shenzhen, Bessent says").

catalysts.title: Reduced Chinese rare‑earth shipments and supplier pivoting
catalysts.description: Decline in Chinese rare‑earth shipments to the US and supplier efforts to test alternatives, altering flows and near‑term resilience.
catalysts.rationale: Chinese rare‑earth shipments to US fell ahead of the summit and suppliers test alternatives ("Chinese rare earth shipments to US drop ahead of Trump-Xi summit", "Aerospace suppliers test rare-earth alternatives").

catalysts.title: Corporate lobbying and industry pressure around summit
catalysts.description: Intense private‑sector advocacy (bank, automaker, tech delegations, CEOs at state events) pushing specific market‑access and protectionist demands.
catalysts.rationale: CEOs attending state dinner and automakers urging bans signal intensive lobbying ("JPMorgan, Citigroup CEOs attending Trump's state dinner", "Automakers Urge Trump Not to Allow Chinese Cars Into U.S.").

catalysts.title: China Central Committee plenum (Oct 26–29)
catalysts.description: Scheduled Party Central Committee plenum that could consolidate domestic posture and recalibrate negotiating stance ahead of follow-ups.
catalysts.rationale: China's Central Committee plenum is scheduled Oct 26–29 and could shape China's negotiating posture ("China's Xi chairs Politburo; Central Committee plenum set for October 26-29").

catalysts.title: Possible LNG tariff adjustments
catalysts.description: Negotiations on cutting tariffs for US LNG ahead of Xi's visit could produce sector‑specific tariff reductions or commitments.
catalysts.rationale: Reports flag US-China talks on cutting tariffs on US LNG ahead of Xi's visit ("US, China discuss cutting tariffs on US LNG ahead of Xi visit").

catalysts.title: Push for U.S.-China AI safety notification system
catalysts.description: US proposal (Bessent) for AI safety notifications could be tabled for agreement or framework commitments at summit or follow-ups.
catalysts.rationale: Treasury's Bessent proposed AI safety notifications and hailed AI dialogue ahead of talks ("Bessent proposes U.S.-China AI safety system", "Scott Bessent hails US-China AI dialogue").
